**Idea 3: batch many phases at once via "cost levels"**: When the marginal cost equals the cost of a specific offer, and each phase pushes 1 unit...

Hmm, what about: for each *request* node, its arcs go to offers; each *offer* has exactly one priced arc. Note the dist of an offer node o is min over r of (dist[r] + pi[r]) - pi[o]... So define M = min over reachable requests of (dist[r] + pi[r]) — then dist[o] = M - pi[o] for offers with any available pair arc from a reachable request. So the Dijkstra essentially needs, for each offer, whether it has a residual pair arc from a *reachable* request. That's still a scan over all pair arcs in the worst case per phase, but the *reachable* set can be much smaller than all requests: after flow saturates, requests already assigned have their in-edge (group→r) saturated... so they're reachable only via reverse pair arcs from offers (rerouting). Hmm, in the late phases most requests are assigned, so the reachable set from the source consists of unassigned requests (few!) plus those reachable via alternating paths.

But note Dijkstra settles nodes in order; the *unassigned* requests are scanned (their pair arcs), and assigned requests are reached only through the alternating structure. In my synthetic worst case (all requests assigned at the end), the number of *unassigned* requests decreases over time but rerouting keeps many reachable.

A practical optimization: when a node's dist > D (limit), we don't need to scan it — handled by early exit ✓.
